newsitem.title: FRANCE: OECD confirms 1997-98 growth seen at 2.5-3.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: OECD confirms 1997-98 growth seen at 2.5-3.0 pct.

text.p: The OECD confirmed in an official communique on Monday evening that it sees growth of 2-5-3.0 percent in 1997-98 and expects it to be more balanced across the 29 OECD member countries.

A draft of the communique obtained by Reuters earlier in the day was unchanged in the final version, which said governments should continue to cut budget deficits and debt and that, given high taxes in many countries, deficit-cutting was likely to have to fall mainly on the spending side.
The communique, like the draft version, said ministers from the 29 OECD countries supported the efforts to achieve a successful introduction of the European single currency.
It said "ministers agreed that fiscal consolidation would continue to be a priority in OECD countries to create the conditions for sustained growth."
"Ministers agreed that improving the quality of expenditure requires increased focus on programmes that contribute to economic growth through enhancing human capital and innovation," it said.
"Continuing reform of public sector management to increase policy effectiveness and expenditure efficiency will also assist in controlling budgets," it said.

"They (ministers) also noted that the pursuit of sound monetary and fiscal policies, combined with continued co-operation on exchange rates, sound financial systems and structural reforms can contribute to smoothly functioning financial markets," it said.
The communique said that "high levels of unemployment will remain in some countries" despite more balanced economic growth across the OECD.
"Ministers confirmed their commitment to pursue policies to achieve strong sustainable non-inflationary growth," it said.

"They recognised that transforming this growth momentum into rising employment will require some differences in the short-run orientation of macroeconomic policies to reflect countries' varying cyclical positions while respecting the medium-term objectives of fiscal consolidation," it said.
